en: Now, I shall duly proclaim the characteristics of the Sadyojāta and other mantras, according to the syllables issued from the limbs of Śiva; listen to that as it is. 1.
O one born from a golden egg, one should place the five names of the Supreme Brahman for the five [limbs]; among these, three are to be known as ending in the dative case.
At the beginning and end is the indication of the action, while at the end of the case-inflection is the name;
the Śaiva [mantra] consists of sixty-eight syllables and is situated beyond the sound *taṅ*.
The fifth [syllable] is the heart; from that, the thirty [syllables] are long and resonant.
The resonant letter *i* is Śaiva; then, after that, is the third.
Then follows his name ending in the dative case with five syllables;
thereafter is the nineteenth [syllable], ending in *ai*, followed by the salutation. || 5 ||
One should place the syllable *va* twice, conjoined with the vowel *e*, as the fruit that is the union of Śiva and the All-Self (Śakti), which is the fourth [tattva] and singular. 6.
From the word *dvirabhyāsa*, one syllable; from *aṣṭama*, the eighth syllable, which is the Śiva-syllable (*ha*);
and thereafter, the final letter of the word *amantraṇa*, which is conjoined with *i*. (7)
First, during the second repetition, omit the final syllable of the word "yogādhipa"; then, from that point, [recite] the first syllable of the next word and its subsequent final syllable.
The eighth word is not defective, as its two final syllables have been elided;
the seventh word from the letter *ja* belongs to Śiva, and from that, the syllable *ā* is the one that has undergone *āmūrchita*.
Then, for the sake of completing the mantra, the wise one should place the fifth syllable, the sixteenth of the seed-mantra, at every step from "uñca" to "muñca," ending with it in the heart.
One should place the second subtle foot above the left foot;
it is distinguished by the letter *e*, and is the first syllable of Rudrāṇī. (11)
From that, the ninth syllable is the infinite Paiṅgala;
one should again place the subtle state (pada) which is formed by the syllables *ta*, *tha*, and *ka*. 12.
The name of Rudra ending in the fourth case (Rudrāya), as well as Trimūrti and Nimi;
from those two, the long Paiṅgala syllable and the pair of letters "kala-kāra. 13.
One should practice as before with those two according to their respective positions; however, in the Gāyatrī, the sixth syllable is Paiṅgala, while the preceding syllable is [the first]. 14.
Then, having removed the syllable situated at the head of the limb of knowledge from that second [syllable],
one should place ten thousand syllables of Śiva located in the letter Ṣa.
Then, following that, one who follows the path of Vāmadeva should establish and place the syllable *ba*, which is of a tawny nature. 16.
Having established the eight letters beginning with *la* there,
the best of those who know the mantra-syllables should make the third one conjoined with the vowel *i*.
Having again established the syllables *ba-la-kā-rā-akṣa-ra-dve* in the Paiṅgala [seat],
one should then place the first [syllable] from those two, followed by the three syllables of the limbs and weapons of the Vidyā.
From the fivefold Śiva, one should place the sixth and then the eighth syllable; from the all-pervading self, one should place the second word thereafter. 19.
One should place the first half of the third word, beginning with "brahmāṇḍa," and the final syllable of the other word. 20.
The third, however, is the Śaiva [state], consisting of twenty-seven [syllables];
it is the end of the third stage, a state following the subtle syllables. || 21 ||
The wise one should place this very subtle word, which is that seed-syllable transformed, as the second syllable within the Gāyatrī.

Therefore, one should perform a prostration to the Trimūrti; following that, one should place the two syllables of *nāda* and *dhana* for the sake of attaining equality with the mantra, as has been further described.
One should place the third syllable after the syllable *bhyo*, which is the weapon-mantra (*astra*) belonging to the limbs of knowledge (*vidyāṅga*);
then, one should again place the triad beginning with the syllable *gho*.
The letters consisting of the Aghora-weapon [are formed] from the seventh and eighth [syllables] of the Aghora-mantra;
then the letter 'a', then the state (bhāva), and again two syllables.
Having established the Paiṅgala syllable consisting of six letters, which is situated above the letter *kā*,
one should assign the two syllables *sarva-kāra* ending with *ekarudra*.
The eleventh [syllable] is the letter *ta* with the visarga, derived from the Aghorāstra mantra;
after that comes the word for the organs of action (*karmendriya*), followed again by *sarva* joined with *bhā*. (27)
From him [were born] the Bhyokāras; therefore, they should be known as belonging to Śiva alone.
From them came the Rudrakāśas, and from them again the Rucas and the Secas. || 28 ||
For the fourth [syllable], however, one should place three syllables beginning with the sixth letter of the Gāyatrī;
likewise, one should again place the word "Mahādeva" ending in the dative case.
Following the three words, there are four syllables of the Gāyatrī ending in "tām";
the last [syllable] and the last of those two, with "sa" in between them—may these Rudras, whose nature is Śiva, be auspicious. 30.
The sixth syllable of the Gāyatrī is "hardi" (in the heart), which is superior to all the gods;
one should place the seventh syllable, "sāyaṃ" (evening), also within the fifth [syllable]. || 31 ||
The eighth syllable is that of Śiva, endowed with the *anacaka*;
the wise one should again place it thereafter, beginning from the region of *yava*.
Then follows the second half of the word *sparśatanmātra*, with the visarga [at its end], and again, within the heart, the two syllables that have the form of the elements. (33)
The Śaiva self, conjoined with the Bindu, is the supreme Brahman of the Śaiva doctrine;
one should install it from the perspective of Vāmadeva as the syllable *ṇa* merged with the syllable *o*.
The two presiding deities of the word *viyat* (space) are those two; from them, the eighth is the subtle, imperishable syllable.
One of these two becomes Brahman. One should place the former [syllable] at the end of the full moon (*rākā*). || 35 ||
One should place Ananteśa in the dharma of the arm ending in the fourth case, and likewise Kṣara; then Stukāra, followed by Śaiva, and Ananteśa as the seventh. (36)
One should then place the syllable ending with Ekarudra and followed by the [syllable] Āmūrcchita;
thereafter, at the end of all, in the fifth and sixth positions, one should place the syllables whose nature is Suśiva.
Three mantras are proclaimed as being joined with the Anuṣṭubh metre;
Vāmadeva, however, is with the Yajus, and the fourth is with the Gāyatrī. (38)
Thus ends the eighth chapter, the Brahma-mantra-paṭala, in the Svāyambhuva-sūtra-saṅgraha.
